FORMAT LINEAGE: Ravena O & Rakesh Gohel (#05, 88 likes) • LangChain OpenWiki
Teaching AI Agents How to Forget: LangChain OpenWiki's Self-Correcting Memory Architecture
Long-lived agents rot when yesterday's true memory becomes today's hallucination. Bind every stored claim to a Git blob SHA receipt.
THE SILENT FAILURE: MEMORY ROT IN LONG-LIVED AGENTS
Most agent memory layers (vector DBs, summary notes) only know how to append. When an engineer
renames a function or updates an API contract, the agent retrieves last month's memory note and
THE LANGCHAIN OPENWIKI FIX: EVIDENCE RECEIPTS + O(1) STALENESS
Never store a naked text summary. Store an Evidence Receipt (file_path, line_span, git_blob_sha).
On retrieval, run a 0-token O(1) hash comparison against current Git HEAD and self-correct stale
claims in the flow of work.
Bind every memory claim to a cryptographic source SHA
When the agent learns an architectural fact,
persist the exact file path, line range, and Git
A claim without a verifiable pointer
Deterministic version check on read (0 LLM tokens)
Before injecting any retrieved memory into the
prompt, compare its stored git_blob_sha against
the current repository tree in <2 ms.
Never ask an LLM 'is this memory still true?'
— hash comparison + git rename detection costs
Preserve historical context while preventing blind trust
architectural intent. Instead, tag the memory as
The stale claim tells the agent *where* to
look; the warning flag stops the agent from
quoting the old number as fact.
Re-read changed span and mint a fresh SHA receipt
During its normal task turn, the agent reads
only the modified lines, updates the memory
claim, and writes the new Git blob SHA.
Memory heals itself on the exact hot paths
VERIFIED BENCHMARK OUTCOMES (LANGCHAIN OPENWIKI • FIRESTORE ⇄ POSTGRESQL + GIT)
Eliminated by mandatory span + SHA receipts
LLM tokens spent on staleness detection
100% deterministic O(1) Git blob SHA lookup
Rule: An agent memory without a source SHA receipt is a future hallucination waiting for the next code commit.
